title: Global Inventory Synchronization for AeroParts
business: AeroParts, a global aerospace logistics provider, manages critical aircraft component inventory across three geographically dispersed data centers.
problem: The company faces significant data inconsistency issues when multiple regional offices attempt to update the same part availability status simultaneously, leading to overselling or phantom inventory errors.
solution: AeroParts implements the Paxos consensus algorithm to ensure that all regional nodes agree on a single, linearizable sequence of inventory updates, preventing conflicting state changes.
steps: Proposer nodes broadcast a proposal with a unique sequence number to all Acceptor nodes.
Acceptors evaluate the proposal and promise to ignore any future requests with lower sequence numbers.
If a majority of Acceptors acknowledge the proposal, the Proposer sends an accept request for the specific value.
Acceptors commit the value if they have not promised to a higher sequence number in the interim.
The system confirms the update as globally consistent once a quorum of Acceptors has successfully stored the value.
outcome: The system achieves a reliable, single-source-of-truth for inventory levels, ensuring that no two regions can commit conflicting updates to the same component record.
limitation: Paxos introduces increased latency due to the multi-phase communication required for quorum agreement; developers can monitor this by tracking the time elapsed between proposal initiation and final commit acknowledgement.

questions.question: In Global Inventory Synchronization for AeroParts, why is Paxos used to address the inventory problem?
options: To ensure all regional nodes agree on a single, linearizable sequence of updates.
To increase the total storage capacity of the regional data centers.
To allow regional offices to update inventory without any network communication.
To automatically delete old inventory records that are no longer needed.
questions.explanation: Paxos is used to maintain consistency across distributed nodes by reaching consensus on a sequence of operations.

questions.question: In Global Inventory Synchronization for AeroParts, what is a primary trade-off associated with the implementation?
options: The system becomes entirely centralized and loses all fault tolerance.
The system experiences increased latency due to the multi-phase communication required for quorum agreement.
The system requires infinite bandwidth to function correctly.
The system cannot handle more than two regional offices.
questions.explanation: The multi-phase nature of Paxos requires multiple round-trips between nodes, which inherently increases latency.
